rules.name: Open Banking API — ASPSP Obligations under PSR 2017
rules.source_legislation: Payment Services Regulations 2017 (PSR 2017) Regs. 68–71; OBIE / Open Banking Ltd API Standards v3.1.x; FCA EMPI supervisory framework
rules.description: As an Account Servicing Payment Service Provider (ASPSP), the bank must maintain Open Banking-compliant APIs enabling authorised AISPs and PISPs to access customer payment accounts with customer consent. APIs must meet OBIE technical standards, be available 99.5%+ of the time, and not introduce unnecessary friction for TPP access. The bank must provide a fallback interface for TPPs if the primary API is unavailable. A quarterly API availability and performance report must be submitted to Open Banking Ltd.
disclosure_obligations: API availability and performance statistics published on the Open Banking Directory quarterly
TPP registration and onboarding process published on the bank's developer portal
Customer-facing consent dashboard showing active AIS and PIS consents with revocation functionality
constraints: API uptime must meet the 99.5% monthly availability threshold — sustained underperformance triggers FCA supervisory engagement
No additional authentication steps beyond those required for direct customer access may be imposed on TPPs
90-day re-authentication must be offered via app-based authentication, not require customers to use online banking
Fallback interface must be available and tested; blocking a fallback is an immediate FCA notification obligation

rules.name: Consumer Duty — Understanding and Consumer Support Outcomes in Digital Channels
rules.source_legislation: FCA Consumer Duty (PS22/9); FCA Guidance FG22/5; FCA Consumer Understanding and Support Outcomes
rules.description: All digital channel designs — including mobile app UX, notification content, product information pages, and customer support routing — must meet the Consumer Duty Understanding and Consumer Support outcomes. Customers must be able to understand the products and services they are using based on digital communications alone. The bank must ensure digital support is accessible, not designed to deter customers from seeking help, and that customers in vulnerable circumstances can access equivalent support digitally or via accessible alternatives.
disclosure_obligations: Annual Consumer Duty assessment for digital channels covering understanding and support outcomes
Accessibility audit results (WCAG 2.1 AA) shared with Head of Compliance and Board
Customer satisfaction and complaint data from digital channels included in Consumer Duty fair value assessments
constraints: Sludge practices (excessive friction in cancellation, complaint, or switching flows) are prohibited under Consumer Duty
Customer support must not be designed to deter customers from making complaints or exercising rights
Digital channels must be accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA standard — failure is treated as a Consumer Duty breach by FCA
Vulnerable customer flags must carry across all digital touchpoints — not reset between sessions

rules.name: Operational Resilience — Digital Banking Important Business Services
rules.source_legislation: FCA PS21/3 (Operational Resilience); PRA SS1/21; Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 Part 5
rules.description: Mobile banking and online banking are designated important business services (IBS). The bank must set board-approved impact tolerances (expressed as maximum acceptable downtime) for each digital IBS, test them against severe-but-plausible disruption scenarios annually, and demonstrate the ability to remain within tolerances. From March 2025, PRA and FCA focus on remediation evidence — banks must have addressed vulnerabilities identified in self-assessments.
disclosure_obligations: Impact tolerance statements for digital banking IBS in the annual operational resilience self-assessment
Material digital service outage reported to FCA within 4 hours (initial) and 24 hours (full report)
Customer communication during sustained IBS breach within prescribed timeframe
constraints: Impact tolerance must be set in terms of maximum continuous downtime and cumulative downtime per rolling 12 months
RTO and RPO targets for digital banking systems must be documented and tested
Critical third-party cloud and CDN providers must be included in resilience scenario testing
Board must review and approve impact tolerances annually — not delegated below Board Risk Committee

rules.name: Variable Recurring Payments (VRP) Commercial Expansion — JROC Roadmap
rules.source_legislation: JROC VRP Roadmap (2023); PSR Variable Recurring Payments policy; FCA cVRP Scheme; PSR 2017
rules.description: The JROC roadmap requires banks to enable commercial VRP (cVRP) beyond sweeping use cases by 2026. The bank must build and expose cVRP APIs within the digital channels layer, surface mandate management to customers in the app and online banking, and ensure its digital consent journey meets FCA cVRP scheme technical requirements. cVRP mandates create a new recurring payment rail that competes with card recurring mandates and BACS direct debits.
disclosure_obligations: Customer-facing cVRP mandate management interface in mobile app and online banking from scheme go-live
Notification to customer when a cVRP mandate is created, amended, or revoked by the PISP
Scheme participation reporting to PSR / FCA per cVRP scheme rules
constraints: cVRP mandate creation must require explicit customer consent through the bank's digital channel
Customer must be able to view, pause, and revoke any cVRP mandate instantly in the app
Payment limits and merchant scope set in the cVRP mandate must be enforced at execution — no override without a new consent

rules.name: UK Digital Identity and Attributes Trust Framework — Identity Relying Party Obligations
rules.source_legislation: DSIT UK Digital Identity and Attributes Trust Framework (DIATF); Data (Use and Access) Act 2025
rules.description: The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 establishes the statutory basis for the UK Digital Identity Trust Framework. The bank as an identity relying party (accepting certified digital identities for onboarding) and potential identity provider must seek DIATF certification. Digital onboarding flows must be updated to accept DIATF-certified identity documents and attributes. This may materially simplify KYC onboarding flows for retail and SME customers and reduce document fraud risk.
disclosure_obligations: DIATF certification status published on the bank's website
Customer-facing disclosure of which digital identity providers the bank accepts
Privacy notice updated to reflect identity attribute data flows under DIATF
constraints: Only DIATF-certified identity providers may be relied upon for identity verification under the framework
Bank cannot use DIATF identity data beyond the purposes consented to by the customer
MLR 2017 CDD obligations are not waived by DIATF identity verification — AML risk assessment must still be completed

rules.name: Smart Data — Investment and Pensions Data Portability APIs
rules.source_legislation: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; FCA Smart Data Scheme Rules (anticipated); HM Treasury Smart Data roadmap
rules.description: Smart Data schemes under the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 will extend Open Banking-style mandatory data portability to investments, pensions, mortgages, and insurance products once FCA makes scheme rules. The bank's digital channels must be enhanced to support broader consent management, API provision for new data categories, and a unified customer data-sharing dashboard covering all in-scope product lines. This is a multi-year investment programme requiring coordination across all capability areas.
approval_chain: Head of Open Banking and Data
disclosure_obligations: Customer data-sharing dashboard in the digital channel covering all Smart Data scheme consents
Annual Smart Data participation report to FCA
Privacy notices updated to reflect each new Smart Data scheme data category added
constraints: Smart Data APIs must be available from scheme commencement date — extensions require FCA approval
Participation is mandatory for banks above the scheme threshold — opt-out not available
Data must be provided in FCA-mandated format and within mandated latency targets
